designStatus: Complete original task-family drafts for source/card/hard-path qualification; no child observations
scope: 56 nongraded shared-stage source positions; grade-column suggested activities are context/examples, not newly mandatory per-grade records.
sourceChoicePolicy: Source-specific form/material/language conditions remain explicit; broad alternatives do not become universal simultaneous mastery requirements.

protocols.title: Body movement, heard cues and actual recall
protocols.task: Prepare a safe clear route and accessible movement options. Show short actual movement patterns associated with contrasting comfortable sounds. For the recall panel, remove the demonstration and ask the learner to recognise the cue and recreate its movement sequence. For instruction coordination, give actual ordered cues and perform the coordinated response. For the gross-motor panel include controlled travelling patterns, jump/landing, still/dynamic balance and a changed direction/space case.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The source-selected panel is actually performed. Recall occurs without merely copying a currently visible adult model; movement is controlled through the required changes, with support/access conditions recorded.
protocols.nearMiss: Naming a movement, moving randomly near music, following a novel cue with no recall check or using a picture of a dancer cannot establish all these duties.
protocols.transfer: Change a sound-to-movement association or safe route, rehearse then check the relevant recall/coordination/transfer again. No fixed athletic ranking or imported sixty-second quota.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Practical care and why it matters
protocols.task: Use real appropriate handwashing/clean-workspace tasks and supplied everyday food, water, rest and movement cases. Ask for a practical caring action and a reason for its contribution to health. Retain the complete existing hygiene/body-needs checks separately, including relevant routine conditions; do not infer a whole habit from one response.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner demonstrates a relevant hygiene action and explains why cleanliness/basic needs matter in the declared case. Appreciation can be recognised value and responsible action without a prescribed pleasant feeling.
protocols.nearMiss: Merely saying “clean is good”, appearance-based body judgments or an adult performing the cleaning does not show the relevant practical/knowledge duty.
protocols.transfer: Use another appropriate routine/case and explain what action is useful and why. Do not add disease diagnosis, adult nutrition prescriptions or a body-shape score.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Recognise and demonstrate surrounding features
protocols.task: Use actual surrounding objects and safe examples with differing orientation, size, colour and material. Ask the learner to identify/show shapes and colours, group or compare examples by a stated feature and explain a meaningful link with an earlier concept. Where a sorting component is tagged, independently check its full classification, counting and category-order operation.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner recognises the source-relevant property in new actual examples, demonstrates it by selection or representation and keeps shape identity stable under orientation/size changes. Separate full-card evidence is retained.
protocols.nearMiss: A colour word alone, matching one memorised picture, sorting only by an irrelevant cue or assuming the sorting count requirement was met by shape naming is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Find another example in a changed setting and explain the same or a different relevant feature. Colour recognition does not require prism/absorption physics.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Source-selected actual visual/material production
protocols.task: Bind the exact required panel: deliberate lines with different tools; actual own clay object and description; purposeful fine control through mark/cut/shape/join tasks; own visual card/poster; actual object printing/impression used in a card/bookmark; or local-art observation and discussion. Perform the declared material/method rather than replacing it with a finished image. Include own visual choices, a deliberate change and new-material/space transfer where the visual-composition claim is tagged.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Actual material handling and the source-selected product/process are present. The imprint panel really transfers an object texture/pattern; clay is actually modelled; an own card/poster contains a purposeful visual arrangement rather than compulsory writing.
protocols.nearMiss: A flat drawing of a clay object, sorting ready-made textures, an adult’s copied poster, printed clip art instead of an actual impression or an unrelated finished craft does not establish the specific panel.
protocols.transfer: Change the available material, working area or intended arrangement and adapt the same required method. No alphabet, one grip, mathematical scale ratio or adult aesthetic norm.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Natural recognition and actual selected sound production
protocols.task: For natural recognition, use accurately attributed locally appropriate animal/weather/water sounds or accessible equivalent descriptions with reliable source identification; identify relevant examples and give an own response. For body production, actually make chosen body sounds and an audible variation. For the small-instrument panel, actually use suitable small instruments to create, listen and purposefully vary a sound arrangement; constructing the instrument is not required.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The exact source panel is sampled: reliable natural-source recognition, actual body-made sound or actual instrument output. Appreciation of nature/body remains a separate contextual channel where printed, with no forced feeling.
protocols.nearMiss: Guessing from a stereotyped picture, body-only output for the instrument position, naming an imagined sound or accepting instrumental output as evidence of body production is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Use another accurately contextualised natural example, a changed body-sound choice or another suitable instrument/expressive intention as appropriate to the panel.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Actual listening, comprehension and instructions
protocols.task: Select the source panel and actual material: a peer’s contribution, a poem/story/nonfiction read aloud, relevant observations discussed in class or a short ordered making/movement instruction sequence. Listen and respond to what was said. For the instruction card, both follow/clarify and give/check clear ordered steps; for read-aloud, ask/answer about real details, discuss meaning and seek clarification as needed. For the listening-observing and classroom-observation-discussion panels, carry out the explicit equipment observation task below: actually inspect two safe known samples using suitable simple equipment, describe details and compare them from observations before the listening/discussion response. It is not enough to discuss observations supplied by an adult.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner’s response uses actual heard content; instruction order and comprehension are demonstrated in the relevant panel. Listening and speaking material is bound to the actual use language without asserting transfer of English phonology or lexical mastery. The observation panels additionally show actual equipment use, an observed detailed description of both samples and an evidence-based similarity/difference comparison, followed by a relevant peer/classroom response.
protocols.nearMiss: Quiet compliance, repeating an adult answer, responding only about one’s own unrelated idea or completing a prepared adult product cannot establish listening/comprehension/instruction use. Merely listening to another person describe a leaf, naming equipment without using it or comparing from a remembered label does not establish the observation panels.
protocols.transfer: Change a contribution, short text or instruction detail and respond appropriately rather than repeat the earlier answer. Whole-card productive and receptive checks remain separate from the source’s narrower duty. For an observation panel, use a new pair of safe samples and actually inspect, describe and compare them with the equipment again.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

equipmentObservationTask.resources: Two safe known leaves, paper pieces or fabric samples, checked for sharp or irritating features; do not collect unknown substances or require organism handling.

learnerActions.instruction: Actually inspect each sample with the selected suitable equipment, adjusting position, focus or light as appropriate to obtain a useful observation.
Describe or record specific observed features such as colour, shape, size, texture or pattern for each sample, pointing to the evidence or using spoken/drawn notes.
Compare the two actually observed samples: identify a relevant similarity and difference and show which observed details support the comparison.
Listen to a partner’s actual observation and respond to its content; in the classroom panel contribute an own observation and reasoned comparison to the discussion.

equipmentObservationTask.transfer: Use another safe sample pair; inspect with the equipment and produce a new observation-based description/comparison, rather than repeat the earlier labels.
equipmentObservationTask.limits: This qualifies the source-specific observation panels and the complete existing observing claim; it is not a new NCERT requirement that every listening/read-aloud task use equipment, and no speed, acuity or diagnosis score is introduced.

protocols.title: Identify local plants and animals accurately
protocols.task: Use a safe direct local observation or accurately prepared accessible record of a local habitat, including a microhabitat. Identify plants and animals by relevant observable features and name suitable examples. Include the full local-card microhabitat/conditions questions separately; do not require handling unknown organisms.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Actual accurately identified local examples and the relevant plant/animal distinctions are demonstrated, with a real habitat/microhabitat relation where the whole card requires it.
protocols.nearMiss: Naming a random animal from a generic poster, inventing a local species occurrence or giving a later taxonomic kingdom list without identifying the actual surroundings does not close this position.
protocols.transfer: Use another local record/setting and explain the identification or relevant habitat difference. Provide background rather than infer universal climate/species lists.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Separate sound properties from the noise-context concept
protocols.task: For the pitch/volume panel use safe actual qualitative high/low and loud/quiet comparisons, then the complete existing source-feature/vibration tasks under controlled conditions. For the sound/noise panel use the approved separate two-context reasoning task: the same gentle sound is wanted for one supplied purpose and interferes in another, while remaining sound. Retain the limited everyday interpretation explicitly; the NCERT table gives no definition.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The selected panel’s concept is explained with reasons and transferred. Pitch is not loudness; contextual unwantedness is not either acoustic dimension, a permanent source label or a universal musical taste rule.
protocols.nearMiss: A physics explanation alone cannot close noise-context reasoning; an opinion about liking a song cannot close the source/vibration claims. Loudness or musical order does not automatically decide the everyday classification.
protocols.transfer: Use a new safe source/context for the declared panel. No actual disturbing exposure, decibel/frequency measurement or technical stochastic-noise course is introduced.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Roles, contributions and respectful everyday action
protocols.task: Use accurately introduced family/community role and work cases, including paid work and unpaid caring roles without conflating them. Identify who does what, how the work contributes and how a role’s duty can change with circumstances. Include an actual respectful/caring response towards people doing different tasks, without ranking their worth by occupation.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner explains contributions and relevant role-duty relationships and demonstrates respectful/helpful action. Appreciation/dignity is not inferred merely from a cheerful tone or naming jobs.
protocols.nearMiss: Calling every family task paid employment, saying some ordinary work makes a person less worthy, describing only job clothes or reciting a polite phrase while excluding someone is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Use a new role/circumstance and recognise the contribution and suitable respectful response. No one profession, caste stereotype or career preference is prescribed.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Describe a feeling without requiring its absence
protocols.task: Use a genuine low-stakes feeling when voluntarily available or a supplied character/artistic situation. Identify and describe the feeling and relevant circumstance, allowing tears or disappointment alongside actual verbal expression. Keep the whole existing revised feeling-expression claim intact; do not manufacture upset or require private disclosure.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner communicates the relevant feeling and situation meaningfully rather than only showing a prescribed facial expression.
protocols.nearMiss: Smiling silently, copying a facial icon without meaning or judging crying as failure cannot establish the expression duty.
protocols.transfer: Use a different ordinary situation or voluntary character response and describe the relevant emotion without demanding a positive mood.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Accurate local arts, celebrations and diverse practices
protocols.task: Bind the source panel: local/folk art and music discussion; cultural awareness/diversity response; family/community celebration comparison; or actual celebration/ritual dramatisation. Use accurately attributed, age-appropriate examples and supply necessary meanings. A voluntarily chosen family case or a supplied anonymous family example can protect privacy. For drama, actually perform the situation and separately retain whole script/poem/improvisation checks. Where the full cultural-diversity claim is assessed, include a respectful actual question and reasoned recognition of another practice, together with the inherited different-life/similarities duties; a fixed cheerful mood or compulsory personal belief disclosure is not inferred.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner recognises relevant practices, discusses actual features/meanings and considers different legitimate examples or responses. Where actual dramatisation is required it occurs, not merely a verbal festival list. Appreciation/interest remains contextual when the source includes that channel.
protocols.nearMiss: Stereotyped culture labels, false attribution, compulsory religious participation, judging one tradition superior or claiming performance mastery from discussion alone is invalid.
protocols.transfer: Use another accurately contextualised practice or expression and compare a meaningful similarity/difference respectfully. No fixed national language/festival pair, private belief disclosure or universal taste.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Actual shared work and another legitimate view
protocols.task: Make a real joint artistic work. Each learner contributes an idea, listens/builds on a peer’s idea and completes a fair part. For peer appreciation/opinion panels, give an own feature-based response, hear a different legitimate response and engage respectfully. For togetherness, provide inclusive shared opportunities and a separate low-stakes reflection rather than inferring a stable feeling.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The shared process contains an actual contribution, relevant response and fair completed work. Disagreement or disappointment can coexist with cooperation and respect.
protocols.nearMiss: Nearby solo work, an adult plan copied without own decisions, compulsory praise or pleasant mood with no contribution does not establish the duty.
protocols.transfer: Change roles, materials or the work under discussion and contribute/respond again. Do not make group membership or cultural agreement conditional on liking every artwork.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Real care for a place, living things and materials
protocols.task: Use a safe school/local nature context and an actual manageable artistic material-use task. Observe plants/animals carefully, identify relevant needs and choose a protective action that avoids disturbing them. Retain appropriate careful minibeast handling/return only when safe and relevant; observing without handling can account for source non-disturbance care where necessary, but does not by itself demonstrate the complete canonical handling operation. An additional safe appropriate handling demonstration is required before certifying that whole minibeast claim. Actually reuse suitable materials or limit waste and explain the effect without inventing a universal zero-impact claim.
protocols.positiveEvidence: A real caring/protective action and suitable resource decision occur, with reasons linked to the place/material/living-thing needs. Source appreciation need not be a compulsory pleasant feeling.
protocols.nearMiss: Only saying “nature is nice”, touching unsafe/unknown animals, making a poster while wasting the supplied materials or claiming a single reused object proves all environmental knowledge is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Use another safe material/place-care case and adapt the action. Whole needs/minibeast/tool checks remain separately assessed, with no advanced carbon accounting or country-specific conservation-course gate.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Selected-form imagination, aesthetic choices and visits
protocols.task: Declare the appropriate accessible selected form and exact source panel. Use a real visual, audible, movement or dramatic production task with own decisions, purposeful comparison/revision and adaptation. For card/poster-or-roleplay, retain the source alternatives rather than making both compulsory. For visit-based work, first actually observe an accessible direct or accurately prepared virtual visit, appraise its real features and creatively represent those observations.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The chosen form’s complete shared claim and required source panel are accounted for; the observation/visit is not invented. Form-specific candidate links remain conditional until the school programme/resources are bound.
protocols.nearMiss: A copied product, an unrelated artwork, an imagined visit represented as observed or claiming all forms mastered from one chosen route is invalid.
protocols.transfer: Change an observed detail, material/resource or expressive intention within the bound programme and adapt. A different chosen art form requires its own binding; no transfer is presumed.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Natural origins and made materials/fibres
protocols.task: Use safe actual objects/material samples or accurate labels and source records. Identify what natural raw material an object is made from, then retain the complete existing natural/made and natural/synthetic-fibre classification checks with suitable examples. Do not confuse the object, its material and the source of that material. Independently retain the inherited fair-test task: compare safe equal-size material samples with equal measured water input, record comparable soak-through observations, repeat/check controls and justify a real-use choice from the actual results; test a changed property separately. This is a canonical hard-path assessment condition, not an added NCERT origin mandate.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner gives a correct origin link and distinguishes relevant natural/made examples, including the whole card’s fibre/processed-material checks rather than inferring them from one basket.
protocols.nearMiss: Only naming a wooden object, calling every manufactured object synthetic, or claiming a made material has no natural source is incomplete.
protocols.transfer: Offer a new safely supplied object/material with adequate information and explain the origin/classification. No extraction, chemistry or industrial-production technique is performed.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Explore, classify, pattern and test bounded claims
protocols.task: Collect or supply safe accurately identified materials and actually observe relevant features. Bind the panel: property classification; material pattern creation; or inquiry/generalisation. Classification includes the full separate sorting/count/category-order checks when tagged. Generalisation requires an own provisional property rule, a new case and an explanation that several confirming observations do not prove every unseen material fits; revise a contradicted rule. For the inherited pattern-spotting claim, also provide an independent exploration opportunity before naming the intended feature/rule and check a prediction from an actually noticed recurrence; a prompted classification alone does not certify that whole claim.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner uses actual observations, classifies by a relevant stated feature and performs the selected pattern/rule task. Own repeating patterns include a real unit/rule, continuation and a new pattern where the whole mathematical claim is tagged.
protocols.nearMiss: Sorting by an unstated irrelevant cue, counting without classification, asserting a universal rule from one object or merely saying a scattered decoration is a formal repeated pattern is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Introduce a new material/example and decide whether the classification or rule still applies. Use safe everyday comparisons, not toxic collection, destructive tests or advanced proof notation.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: A real conceptual link and strategy used elsewhere
protocols.task: After meaningful Arts and another subject task, ask for a specific connection between a new idea and prior knowledge. Then provide a genuinely different task where a previously learned strategy can help, such as organising observations for a making plan. The learner identifies and actually uses the strategy, with relevant prior/planning checks separately retained. No genuine gap, frustration, positive feeling or whole metacognitive-chain attainment is manufactured or inferred from artistic task success; assess inherited whole claims separately in their own appropriate circumstances.
protocols.positiveEvidence: There is an explained relation and an enacted useful transfer, not merely mention of two school subject names.
protocols.nearMiss: Repeating an adult analogy, labelling an artwork “maths” without a relation, or claiming transfer while using an unrelated strategy is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Use another different context and explain what carries over and what needs adapting; similarity of surface materials alone does not establish transfer.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Own ending, actual tableau and group drama
protocols.task: Bind the required panel: create a coherent own story completion; depict a situation as a non-speaking embodied still image/tableau; or actually dramatise a story with a group. Preserve the whole unchanged story-adaptation claim with familiar-original retelling and a changed character/setting/ending, and the whole theatre claim with script, poem and improvisation plus purposeful voice/action/silence/stillness where tagged.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner actually performs the required source operation. A tableau has an embodied dramatic relationship, a meaningful changed pose/relation and an indicated interpretation; the group scene has actual roles/contributions.
protocols.nearMiss: A drawn picture standing for a tableau, a repeated adult ending, a flat retelling or a single pose offered as proof of the entire scripts-and-poetry claim is incomplete.
protocols.transfer: Change the fictional situation, ending or character relationship and perform/adapt meaningfully. No independent-reading, personal-trauma or compulsory cultural-role disclosure gate is introduced.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Plan, gather, execute and check actual work
protocols.task: Give a manageable real artistic task with genuine resource and order choices. Let the learner identify steps, gather what is needed, carry out the sequence and review the result. Separately check the whole planning/checking criteria and distinguish preparation from merely obeying an adult’s completed plan. No genuine gap, frustration, positive feeling or whole metacognitive-chain attainment is manufactured or inferred from artistic task success; assess inherited whole claims separately in their own appropriate circumstances.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner makes an own usable plan, gathers relevant resources and checks whether the result fits the intention, revising where a real discrepancy occurs.
protocols.nearMiss: A tidy table prepared by an adult, reciting numbered steps without using them or manufacturing an error to force a correction does not establish independent organisation.
protocols.transfer: Change a resource/constraint and plan an appropriate adaptation; no universal efficiency, speed or adult-perfect tidiness score.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Words acquired and actually used in the use language
protocols.task: Use an actual Arts conversation/read-aloud and relevant material/context to introduce needed words. The learner then uses them meaningfully in their own speech and writing and a changed context, with age-appropriate access support that does not silently replace the productive duty. Bind the real language/material vocabulary for use; no national language pair is chosen.
protocols.positiveEvidence: New relevant words are used appropriately rather than only repeated/defined, and both speech and writing parts of the unchanged complete shared-operation claim are checked separately.
protocols.nearMiss: A copied glossary, one adult-completed label, English words inferred from non-English activity or one repeated definition cannot establish functional use.
protocols.transfer: Use a new relevant artwork/material/context and apply the words appropriately. No universal vocabulary size or automatic script/orthography transfer.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

protocols.title: Retained enjoyment without a compliance score
protocols.task: Provide safe accessible varied artistic opportunities, genuine choices and optional reflection about what was enjoyable, difficult, worthwhile or not preferred in this task. Retain the printed enjoyment position as a contextual curriculum requirement with no binary mastery topic or inference that every learner must like every activity.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The authoring design includes the opportunity/voice/support channel and recognises that enjoyment varies by task and time. No child feeling or success is claimed from this report.
protocols.nearMiss: Compulsory smiling, absence of frustration, praise of every art form or an adult inferring liking from compliance is invalid evidence.
protocols.transfer: Offer another supported choice and voluntary reflection; actual production/knowledge tasks remain assessed elsewhere and are not replaced by positive feelings.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit task design, not actual learner observations or intervention efficacy.

sourceBindings.sourceInterpretation: Bounded everyday contextual unwanted/interfering-sound interpretation; not claimed to be an explicit NCERT publisher definition. Actual surrounding source and complete pinned-source text contain no contrary ordered/irregular-vibration definition.
